---
title: "Get started with quartodown"
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Get started with quartodown}
  %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

quartodown builds a pkgdown-style website for an R package with
[Quarto](https://quarto.org/). This guide sets up a package, builds its site,
and publishes it on GitHub Pages.

## Set up

From the root of your package, run:

```r
quartodown::use_quartodown()
```

This writes `_quartodown.yml` at the package root, the one configuration file
you edit, and adds the files the build generates to `.gitignore` and
`.Rbuildignore`. The configuration file is optional: without it, the site is
built with the defaults.

## Build the site

```r
quartodown::build_site()
quartodown::preview_site()
```

`build_site()` builds the site into `docs/`, and `preview_site()` opens it in
your browser.

::: {.callout-tip}
Examples in the man pages and code in the vignettes run against your package's
current source: `build_site()` installs it into a temporary library first. To
skip the install while iterating, use `build_site(devel = TRUE)`, which loads it
with `pkgload::load_all()` instead.
:::

The site is built from what's already in your package:

- **Home page**: `README.md`, with a sidebar of links, the license, citation and
  developers taken from `DESCRIPTION`. Badges between `<!-- badges: start -->`
  and `<!-- badges: end -->` move into the sidebar.
- **Reference**: one page per `man/*.Rd` file, and an index of them.
- **Get started**: the vignette named after the package, like this one.
- **Articles**: every other vignette, including those in `vignettes/articles/`.
- **Changelog**: `NEWS.md`, with issues (`#123`) and GitHub users (`@user`)
  linked.

## Organize the reference index

By default the reference index lists every function in one section. To group
them, edit the `reference:` field in `_quartodown.yml`. It has the same shape as
pkgdown's:

```yaml
reference:
  - title: Setting up
    contents:
      - use_quartodown
  - title: Building
    contents:
      - starts_with("build_")
```

`?build_site` lists the other fields: `articles:` sets the order of the
"Articles" menu, and `quarto:` changes the Quarto configuration, e.g. to add
navbar links.

## Publish on GitHub Pages

This GitHub Actions workflow builds the site and deploys it to the `gh-pages`
branch on every push. Save it as `.github/workflows/quartodown.yaml`:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:

name: quartodown

jobs:
  quartodown:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: quartodown-${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.run_id }}
    env:
      GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          use-public-rspm: true

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          extra-packages: any::knitr, any::rmarkdown, github::BjarkeHautop/quartodown, local::.
          needs: website

      - name: Build site
        run: quartodown::build_site()
        shell: Rscript {0}

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4
        with:
          clean: false
          branch: gh-pages
          folder: docs
```

`local::.` installs your package's dependencies, which its examples and
vignettes need. Then, on GitHub, set the repository to serve Pages from the
`gh-pages` branch (*Settings* → *Pages*).

[Technical
